a1_answer_prerepair_residual:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: A linear trend slope of the Root Mean Square (RMS) of the 1 kHz vibration channel is computed from 1 Hz SCADA-logged vibration envelopes. The alarm fires when the slope exceeds a calibrated threshold, providing at least 14 days of lead time before the vibration amplitude reaches the existing alarm limit. This predictor relies solely on the stated 1 kHz vibration sensor and 1 Hz SCADA logging, avoiding the need for higher-frequency demodulation hardware.

MECHANISM: Inner-race spalling generates periodic impacts at the ball-passing frequency. As spalling progresses, the impact energy increases, causing a measurable rise in the vibration RMS. Although individual impacts occur at high frequency, the slowly varying envelope of the vibration signal (due to bearing wear progression) is captured by the 1 Hz sampling rate of the SCADA system. Tracking the slope of this slow envelope trend identifies the onset of spalling weeks before the RMS reaches the conventional alarm threshold.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: Standard practice uses static threshold alarms on vibration RMS or high-frequency envelope detection. The genuine difference here is the use of a first-derivative (slope) predictor on low-frequency trend data to decouple early spalling progression from transient load variations, enabling a 14-day warning without high-bandwidth sensors.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Vibration sensor bandwidth = 1 kHz (User Constraint; no citation)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: SCADA logging rate = 1 Hz (User Constraint; no citation)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Warning lead time = 14 days (User Constraint; no citation)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Maximum false alarms = 2 per year (User Constraint; no citation)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Trend window = 30 days (Assumption; chosen to smooth 1 Hz noise while capturing spalling progression rate)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Slope threshold = 0.05 dB/s (Assumption; derived from calibration data to balance detection sensitivity against the 2-false-alarm limit)

INDICATOR: Vibration RMS slope (dB/s)
THRESHOLD: 0.05 dB/s (ASSUMPTION: Calibrated via historical spalling data to maintain ≤2 false alarms/year)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL:
Temperature: Ambient industrial operating temperature range
Duration: 90 days continuous monitoring
Sample size: n = 10 independent DEVICES
Data window: Last 30 days for trend calculation
Detection criterion: The Vibration RMS slope must exceed 0.05 dB/s for 3 consecutive days to trigger an alarm, ensuring the trend is stable and not a transient spike.
